pulmonary_angiography.summary: Pulmonary angiography has procedure-related risks. In a study of 1111 patients, mortality and complication rates were low but present; contrast use should be minimized and non-selective injections avoided in haemodynamically compromised patients.
pulmonary_angiography.clinical_notes: Majority of deaths occurred in patients with haemodynamic compromise or respiratory failure. The amount of contrast agent should be reduced and non-selective injections avoided in patients with haemodynamic compromise. Strengths/weaknesses and radiation issues summarized in Table 6 (referenced).

magnetic_resonance_angiography.summary: MRA has been evaluated for suspected PE but large-scale studies show limited sensitivity, a high proportion of inconclusive scans, and low availability in emergency settings; thus it is not yet ready for routine clinical practice. A negative MRA combined with absence of proximal DVT on compression ultrasonography is being investigated as a rule-out strategy for clinically significant PE.
limitations: Low availability in most emergency settings

ongoing_investigation.description: Hypothesis that negative MRA + absence of proximal DVT on compression ultrasonography may safely rule out clinically significant PE

echocardiography.summary: Echocardiography can detect RV pressure overload and dysfunction caused by acute PE, but no single echocardiographic parameter reliably provides RV size or function information. Reported negative predictive value is limited, so a negative echocardiogram cannot exclude PE. Specific echocardiographic signs (e.g., RV dilatation, pulmonary ejection acceleration time <60 ms, peak systolic tricuspid valve gradient thresholds, McConnell sign, depressed RV free wall contractility) may support diagnosis but are present only in a subset of patients and can be seen with other cardiac/respiratory disease.

findings_and_performance.notes_on_specific_signs: Combination of pulmonary ejection acceleration time <60 ms with a low peak systolic tricuspid valve gradient or depressed RV free wall contractility (McConnell sign) is suggestive of PE but present only in a minority of unselected PE patients (reported figures referenced in text).
limitations: Signs of RV overload or dysfunction may be found in absence of acute PE (concomitant cardiac or respiratory disease)
Echocardiography may show misleading incidental findings (e.g., LV systolic dysfunction or valvular disease)
findings_and_performance.utility: Helps distinguish acute PE from RV free wall hypokinesia/akinesia due to RV infarction; aids risk stratification when RV dilation or dysfunction present.
